title: Analyzing Active Fund Managers' Commitment to ESG: Evidence from the United Nations Principles for Responsible Investment
eligible_reason: Binary treatment (mutual fund's management company signs the UN PRI) switches on at fund-specific quarters: 45 distinct first-treated quarters, signing years 2006-2017. Regressions are reghdfe y post_pri if j>-8 & j<6, a(wficn1 yearqtr) cluster(wficn1) with no covariates (fund FE + calendar-quarter FE), plus dynamic versions with post-only relative-quarter indicators t_plus1..t_plus6. The estimation window holds only signatory funds, so not-yet-signed funds are the controls; untreated observations exist in 46 of the 47 treated calendar quarters. Annual voting regressions (Table 6 Panel D) use the same structure with fund and year FE. All analysis files are shipped.
design_notes: Fund-quarter panel xsectionalanalysis.dta (3,034 funds; window sample opentonewinv==1 & -7<=j<=5: 5,245 obs, 595 funds; TVL score N = 4,041). j = quarter relative to signing (0 = signing quarter); post = 1{j>=0}; pri = 1 for all window rows; post_pri is stored and equals post*pri. t_plus1..t_plus6 = 1{j=0}..1{j=5}; t = 1{j=-1}, unused. Outcomes are fund value-weighted ESG scores (TVL fullscore/matscore, MSCI was/ias, Sustainalytics) built in SAS from licensed holdings and ESG data. Derivative files for Tables 5-6 (entry/exit, top/bottom quartile shares, controversies, bottom performers, improvement) share the same panel keys. The first reghdfe in several do-files (year on post_pri) is a sanity check. Tables 3 and 7 restrict the sample to e(sample) of a regression that includes quarterlyret, logfundsize or fullscore_alt, which is a non-missing restriction only. Table 8 interacts post with fund-type splits (excluded). Table 6 Panel C is a firm-level continuous-ownership regression with controls (excluded).
n_eligible_specs_note: Counts every coded no-control column with post_pri, post, or t_plus bins: Table 3 (2), Table 4 (3 static + 5 dynamic), Table 5 Panel A (6), Panel B (12), Panel C (16), Panel D (6), Table 6 Panel A (6), Panel B (6), Panel D (10), Table 7 (4). Table and panel mapping comes from the package folder names (no article text); verify against the published tables, especially whether the dynamic columns and matscore/ias are main-text.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: 45 distinct first-treated yearqtr among 579 funds observed post-signing in the window (computed from xsectionalanalysis.dta). By signing year: 2006 44, 2007 72, 2008 70, 2009 39, 2010 28, 2011 68, 2012 105, 2013 51, 2014 40, 2015 56, 2016 12, 2017 10 funds. 16 funds appear only pre-signing in the window. Voting file: 12 first-post years (2007-2018).

data_access: partial (fund-level analysis files shipped; raw CRSP, Thomson, ISS, MSCI, Sustainalytics and TVL inputs are licensed and not included)
data_files_note: readme.pdf: analysis files are uploaded and are the real aggregated values (no masking or noise mentioned). Note that winsor2 runs before keep if opentonewinv==1, so winsorized flow cutoffs use the full file.
software_notes: Stata reghdfe (keepsing), winsor2; SAS for data construction. Logs shipped as PDF and .log.
priority_note: Eligible, real data shipped, Stata. Caveats: treated-only window sample (identification from not-yet-treated funds, so the last cohorts have thin controls); event windows trimmed at -7..+5 quarters; keepsing retains singletons; event bins are post-only with pooled pre reference.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text). Verified in Python from the shipped .dta files: post_pri == post*pri on the window sample; pri == 1 for all window rows; no switch-offs; cohort counts as above; window N for TVL score = 4,041, matching the log. The large .dta files were read column-subset only.
